title: Using a Peristaltic Pump to Flow Buffer Through a Nanoporous Membrane
author: Harley King
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rwqd7dw

steps.title: Prepare and Prime Filter Assembly
steps.instruction: Prepare the filter assembly and prime the tubing using the chosen buffer.

substeps.instruction: Insert a teflon ring into the luer-lock end half of the filter assembly.
Connect both halves of the filter assembly without a membrane, ensuring a tight connection so the teflon ring is properly seated.
Connect the assembly to a peristaltic pump with flow directed towards the reinforced end.
Use the 'prime' or a fast flow setting on the pump to wash the tubing and filter holder for several seconds using the buffer of choice.

steps.title: Load Membrane into Assembly
steps.instruction: Carefully place the membrane into the luer-lock end of the assembly.

substeps.instruction: Unscrew the filter holder assembly.
Use a transfer pipette to add buffer dropwise to the luer-lock end half until a slight positive meniscus forms above the teflon ring, using a gloved finger to prevent leakage.
Transfer the membrane into the reservoir in the luer-lock end using padded or paper forceps.
Gently nudge the membrane into place against the ring using a transfer pipette or an impermeable, padded membrane.
Screw the reinforced side into the luer-lock end until finger tight, proceeding slowly to ensure the reinforced end properly seats the membrane against the ring.

steps.title: Initialize Flow
steps.instruction: Integrate the assembly into the flow line and initiate buffer flow.

substeps.instruction: Use a transfer pipette to add fluid to each side of the filter assembly to create a positive meniscus.
Insert the filter assembly into the flow line.

steps.title: Operate Buffer Flow
steps.instruction: Flow buffer through the membrane at the appropriate rate for the duration of the experiment.

substeps.instruction: Set the flow rate; for SmartPor25 alumina membranes (50μM thick), use 0.1mL (note: 0.5 ml/min is too high and may crack the membrane). For other membranes, determine the flow rate empirically.
Verify that buffer exits the tip from the reinforced end (drop formation may take several minutes at slow rates).
Ensure no fluid escapes between the interfaces of the filter assembly halves; if leakage occurs, tighten the halves carefully or reduce pressure.
Continue flow for 1-2 hours.
Optional: A syringe pump may be used instead of a peristaltic pump.
Optional: Estimate flow rate by observing the volume that fills a microcentrifuge tube in 1 minute.

steps.title: Recover Membrane
steps.instruction: Detach the assembly and carefully remove the membrane for study.

substeps.instruction: Detach the filter assembly from the flow line.
Unscrew the two halves of the filter assembly in a counter-clockwise manner.
If the membrane is stuck to the luer-lock side, invert it onto parafilm or another impermeable surface.
Place a few drops of buffer through the luer-lock side onto the stuck membrane using a transfer pipette and nudge it away from the luer-lock end with the pipette tip.
If the teflon ring sticks to the membrane, use the transfer pipette and padded forceps to push the membrane down while tugging the ring to separate them.
Remove excess fluid using a transfer pipette; do not blot with a wipe.
Mount the membrane onto the material of choice for study.
